topic: Passive consumption loops and the wanting/pleasure dopamine split
body:
**You watched three hours of content you didn't even enjoy. And you'll do it again tonight.**

This is the most important distinction in the whole dopamine conversation. Dopamine is not the pleasure chemical — it's the wanting chemical. Your brain releases it in anticipation of reward, not in response to it. That's why you keep scrolling even when nothing is satisfying you. You're not chasing pleasure. You're chasing the search for it.

The feed is engineered for this. The next video might be the one. The next post might hit. Your brain knows this isn't working — and it keeps going anyway, because the mechanism that drives behaviour is want, not satisfaction.

This is why you feel worse after three hours of passive consumption. You've flooded the wanting system and received almost nothing back. The account is overdrawn.

Enjoyment and engagement are not the same signal. If you can't remember what you watched, you weren't resting. You were numbing. Those require different responses.

Full breakdown in the link in bio.
